Under a label-free viral-replication growth selection, near-isosteric polar swaps are the class least likely to perturb folding, packing, or protein-protein interfaces, so predicted fitness stays closest to (or marginally above) wild type. No structural or assay evidence was consulted; this is a chemistry-and-substitution-class prior only.","evidence":[],"validation":[],"would_overturn":"A measured replication/growth readout showing T192S at or below the deleterious cutoff, or structural/mechanistic information placing residue 192 in a hydroxyl-methyl-dependent contact (e.g., a Thr-specific gamma-methyl packing or phosphosite) where Ser cannot substitute."},{"rank":2,"mutant":"I315V","basis":"Ile->Val preserves beta-branched aliphatic character and loses only a single methylene, a classic tolerated hydrophobic-core substitution. Small-volume-decrease swaps within the same chemical class rarely abolish replication competence, so this ranks near the top on substitution-class plausibility alone.","evidence":[],"validation":[],"would_overturn":"Replication data showing a fitness drop for I315V, or evidence that position 315 sits in a tightly packed cavity where the lost methyl creates a destabilizing void, or that Ile315 is part of a beta-branch-dependent specificity pocket."},{"rank":3,"mutant":"V152I","basis":"Val->Ile is the reciprocal conservative aliphatic swap, adding one methylene while keeping beta-branching. Such additions are frequently neutral and occasionally stabilizing, which fits a 'higher values preferred' fitness direction. Positions near a construct terminus are, as a prior, more permissive because they are less likely to be part of the folded core or a conserved active site. Both factors point to a near-neutral replication phenotype.","evidence":[],"validation":[],"would_overturn":"Growth/replication data showing V35L is deleterious, or information that the N-terminal segment of this construct is structured and that Val35 packs in a beta-branch-specific manner rather than being terminal and flexible."},{"rank":5,"mutant":"L555M","basis":"Leu->Met is a well-tolerated hydrophobic exchange of similar volume; Met is flexible and readily substitutes for Leu at buried and interface positions. Predicted to preserve fold and therefore replication fitness. No position-specific data was used.","evidence":[],"validation":[],"would_overturn":"A measured fitness decrement for L555M, or evidence that residue 555 requires branched-aliphatic geometry, or that an added methionine is oxidation-sensitive or creates an unwanted internal initiation/processing liability in this construct."},{"rank":6,"mutant":"D621E","basis":"Asp->Glu conserves negative charge and carboxylate chemistry, extending the side chain by one methylene. This is among the safest charged-residue substitutions and typically neutral at surface positions, which dominate the prior for an unannotated site.","evidence":[],"validation":[],"would_overturn":"Replication data showing loss of fitness, or evidence that Asp621 is a catalytic or metal/ion-coordinating aspartate with strict geometric requirements that the longer glutamate cannot satisfy."},{"rank":7,"mutant":"I291M","basis":"Ile->Met is another same-class hydrophobic swap preserving overall bulk and burial preference. reasons."},{"mutant":"L576F","reason":"Hydrophobic-to-aromatic swap keeps burial preference but increases bulk and rigidity, a common source of packing strain in a interfaces."},{"mutant":"A69R","reason":"Introduces a large basic side chain where a minimal one existed; high steric and electrostatic perturbation if the position is at all substantial shortening; risky for a replication-relevant interface."},{"mutant":"Q411K","reason":"Introduces a positive charge in place of a neutral amide of similar length; electrostatic change sites."},{"mutant":"R574A","reason":"Arginine-to-alanine deletes charge, bulk, and hydrogen bonding at once, one of the more disruptive surface substitutions aromatic replacing a small beta-branched aliphatic, a substantial steric insult at a likely packed position."},{"mutant":"V64C","reason":"Introduces a free thiol capable of aberrant disulfide change."},{"mutant":"I548C","reason":"Replaces a bulky aliphatic with a smaller reactive thiol, combining cavity formation with aberrant-disulfide risk."},{"mutant":"L649C","reason":"Loses hydrophobic 673 is near the 691 construct end but still within the folded region; buried-charge penalty dominates."},{"mutant":"I673Y","reason":"Bulky hydroxylated aromatic replacing a beta-branched aliphatic; volume increase makes this among the least plausible substitutions there."},{"mutant":"G680N","reason":"Glycine-to-amide substitution removes essential backbone flexibility and adds bulk; conserved glycines rarely tolerate side-chain addition."},{"mutant":"G420H","reason":"Places a bulky titratable aromatic at a glycine position, a combination of steric intrusion and lost backbone site."},{"mutant":"Y377T","reason":"Deletes a large aromatic and its hydroxyl, leaving a cavity and losing both stacking and hydrogen-bonding contributions."},{"mutant":"W585I","reason":"Tryptophan severe."},{"mutant":"C378Y","reason":"Cysteine deletion with possible disulfide loss plus a large aromatic substitution; compounded structural risk."},{"mutant":"Q532P","reason":"Proline introduction
